name: kev-is-always-p1
rule: Any CVE added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog is P1 CRITICAL regardless of CVSS score. KEV means confirmed active exploitation in the wild with federal remediation deadlines.
evidence: CISA KEV entries have confirmed exploitation. This is the highest-confidence signal in threat intelligence.

name: epss-above-07-escalate
rule: When EPSS score exceeds 0.7, escalate to at least P2 regardless of whether a public exploit exists. EPSS > 0.7 indicates high probability of exploitation within 30 days based on statistical models trained on real exploitation data.

name: high-risk-vendor-escalation
rule: CVEs affecting Ivanti, Fortinet, Citrix, Palo Alto Networks, and SolarWinds should receive a +1 priority escalation. These vendors have a documented history of rapid exploitation — often within days of disclosure. A CVSS 7.5 for Ivanti carries more real-world risk than CVSS 7.5 for a niche product.

name: rce-unauthenticated-is-p1
rule: CVEs with 'remote code execution' AND ('unauthenticated' OR 'no user interaction') in the description should be P1 if CVSS >= 8.0. These indicate trivially exploitable vulnerabilities that require no prerequisites.

name: poc-published-escalate
rule: When a public exploit or proof-of-concept is published on GitHub for a CVE, escalate by one priority level. The existence of weaponised code dramatically increases the probability and speed of exploitation.

name: unexpected-certificate-is-p2
rule: New SSL certificates issued for monitored domains from unexpected Certificate Authorities, or for unexpected subdomains, should be flagged as P2. This can indicate phishing infrastructure, shadow IT, or CA compromise.

name: dmarc-none-is-p1
rule: A monitored domain with DMARC policy p=none or missing DMARC record is P1 for email security. This means anyone can send email impersonating the domain with no enforcement. Combined with SPF softfail (~all), the domain is fully spoofable.

name: supply-chain-malware-is-p1
rule: Any GitHub Advisory tagged as 'malware' or any advisory involving a poisoned dependency is P1 CRITICAL. Supply chain attacks affect every downstream consumer of the compromised package. Check if affected packages are in client tech stacks immediately.

name: patch-tuesday-tracking
rule: Microsoft Patch Tuesday releases (second Tuesday of each month) should trigger a focused review of all Microsoft CVEs. CVEs in Exchange, SharePoint, Entra ID, and Intune affecting monitored stacks are P2 minimum on release day.

name: correlation-escalation
rule: When multiple risk signals co-occur for the same CVE (high CVSS + high EPSS, or CVE + public exploit + scanning activity, or CVE + vendor in KEV history), the combined risk exceeds any single signal. Escalate by one priority level when 2+ risk signals are present.
